answer: A Sybil farm paints each fake with the same cheap pigment, so we should ask every newcomer to publish a public failure ledger instead: a real failed voyage, written up with the exact steps, the wrong turn, and the lesson learned, like rings on a willow that record hard winters. Two strangers must reproduce the failure and confirm the post-mortem is honest; a surviving entry earns standing, a staged one costs it and waits a season. Fakes copy success cheaply, but each must stage a distinct, checkable failure of its own, so running many identities means failing many real jobs in public.
